description: Deterministic security rules for reinhardt, mapped to OWASP. Maintained separately from the engine; every rule ships positive and negative test vectors that the engine test suite must execute.
disclaimer: Heuristic static patterns. A match is a lead for verification, not proof of a vulnerability; no match is not evidence of safety.
vector_format: tests.positive/negative are {path, text, with?}. text may be an array of strings joined with no separator (used so credential-shaped samples never appear contiguously in this file). with lists extra files present in the same repository.
repo_any_format: Optional per-rule gate evaluated before anything else: the rule runs only if at least one scanned candidate file path matches a repo_any.paths regex OR at least one candidate file text matches a repo_any.text pattern {regex, flags}. Applies to every kind, including supabase-rls. Test vectors are evaluated as a repository consisting of the vector file plus its with files.
ref_format: <standard-id>:<item-id> resolving to data/owasp/<standard-id>.json items[].id (split on the FIRST colon only). asvs entries are version-pinned ASVS 5.0.0 L1 requirement ids.

rules.title: Live credential committed to the repository
rules.detail: A string matching a documented provider credential format appears in tracked source. Anything committed must be treated as exposed, including in git history and in shipped client bundles.
rules.suggested_fix: Revoke and rotate the credential first, then remove it from the code, load it from a server-side secret store or environment variable, and purge it from history if the repository is or was public.

rules.title: Secret read through a client-exposed environment variable
rules.detail: Framework prefixes such as NEXT_PUBLIC_, VITE_, EXPO_PUBLIC_ and REACT_APP_ inline the value into the browser or app bundle, where anyone can read it. The variable name indicates a server-only secret (service-role key, model-provider key, private key or database URL).
rules.suggested_fix: Rename the variable without the public prefix, read it only in server code (route handler, server action, edge function), and rotate the value because previously built bundles already contain it.

rules.title: LLM provider SDK enabled in the browser
rules.detail: The OpenAI and Anthropic JavaScript SDKs refuse to run in a browser unless dangerouslyAllowBrowser is true, because the API key then ships to every visitor, who can spend against it without limits.
rules.suggested_fix: Call the model from a server route that holds the key, authenticates the user, and enforces rate limits and output-token caps; remove dangerouslyAllowBrowser and rotate the exposed key.

positive.text: const openai = new OpenAI({ apiKey, dangerouslyAllowBrowser: true });

negative.text: const openai = new OpenAI({ apiKey, dangerouslyAllowBrowser: false });

rules.title: Supabase privileged key referenced in client code
rules.detail: Supabase service_role and sb_secret_ keys bypass Row Level Security. Referencing one from a client component, mobile view or browser framework file means every user can read and write every row.
rules.suggested_fix: Use only the anon or publishable key on clients; move privileged operations to a server route or Edge Function that checks the caller and uses the secret key there. Rotate the key if it was ever bundled.

positive.text: let client = SupabaseClient(supabaseURL: url, supabaseKey: Secrets.service_role)

rules.title: Supabase table created without Row Level Security
rules.detail: A table in the public (API-exposed) schema is created in a migration, but no SQL file enables Row Level Security on it. With the anon key shipped to clients, anyone can query the table through the auto-generated API.
rules.suggested_fix: Add `alter table <name> enable row level security;` and owner-scoped policies (for example `using (auth.uid() = user_id)`), or move the table to a schema that is not exposed.
rules.algorithm: Collect every `create table [if not exists] [public.]<name>` in .sql files (schema omitted or public; quoted names allowed, compare case-insensitively without quotes). Collect every `alter table [only] [if exists] [public.]<name> enable row level security` across all .sql files. Report each created table that never has RLS enabled; evidence is the create statement line.

positive.text:
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS "Notes" (id int);
alter table profiles enable row level security;

negative.text:
create table public.profiles (id uuid primary key);
alter table public.profiles enable row level security;
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS "User" (id uuid primary key);

rules.title: Supabase write policy allows every row
rules.detail: A Row Level Security policy for write operations uses `true` as its condition, so any role the policy applies to can modify any row. RLS is enabled but provides no ownership check.
rules.suggested_fix: Scope the policy to the owner, e.g. `using (auth.uid() = user_id) with check (auth.uid() = user_id)`, and restrict it `to authenticated`.

positive.text: create policy "edit" on posts for update using (true);

negative.text:
create policy "read" on posts for select using (true);
create policy "edit" on posts for update using (auth.uid() = author_id);

rules.title: Firebase security rules allow unrestricted access
rules.detail: Firestore, Storage or Realtime Database rules grant access with no condition, `if true`, or the expiring test-mode rule. The Firebase client config is public by design, so these rules are the only access control.
rules.suggested_fix: Deny by default and grant per document, e.g. `allow read, write: if request.auth != null && request.auth.uid == resource.data.ownerId;`. Note that `request.auth != null` alone still exposes every user's data to every signed-in user.

positive.text: allow read, write: if request.time < timestamp.date(2026, 11, 1);

negative.text: allow read, write: if request.auth != null && request.auth.uid == userId;

rules.title: Request body written directly to the database
rules.detail: The whole client-supplied body is passed to a create/update call, so a user can set fields they should not control, such as role, is_admin, owner id or price.
rules.suggested_fix: Validate the body with a schema (zod, valibot) and copy only allow-listed fields; set ownership and privilege fields on the server.

positive.text: await prisma.post.update({ where: { id }, data: req.body })

rules.title: CORS allows credentials from any origin
rules.detail: CORS is configured with credentials and an origin of `*` or `true` (reflect any origin). Any website can then make authenticated requests on behalf of a signed-in user and read the responses.
rules.suggested_fix: Use an explicit allow-list of trusted origins when credentials are enabled.

rules.title: Redirect target taken from the request
rules.detail: The redirect destination comes from a query, body or route parameter, which lets attackers craft links on your domain that forward victims to phishing pages or leak OAuth codes.
rules.suggested_fix: Redirect only to relative paths or to destinations on an allow-list; reject absolute URLs and protocol-relative `//` values.

rules.title: Server fetches a URL supplied by the request
rules.detail: A server-side HTTP request uses a URL or host from the incoming request. Attackers can make the server reach internal services or cloud metadata endpoints (169.254.169.254).
rules.suggested_fix: Allow-list destination hosts, resolve and block private/link-local addresses, and disable automatic redirect following for user-influenced requests.

rules.title: SQL query built with string interpolation
rules.detail: Values are interpolated into SQL text instead of being passed as parameters, so input containing quotes or SQL can change the query.
rules.suggested_fix: Use parameter placeholders ($1, ?) with a values array, a tagged template that parameterizes (sql``, Prisma $queryRaw``), or the query builder.

positive.text: await pool.query(`SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ${req.params.id}`);
db.query("SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = '" + email + "'")

negative.text: await pool.query('SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = $1', [id]);
await prisma.$queryRaw`SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ${id}`
await sql`select * from users where id = ${id}`

rules.title: MongoDB query built from strings or raw request objects
rules.detail: A MongoDB `$where` clause is assembled from strings (server-side JavaScript evaluation), or a whole request object is used as a query filter, letting clients inject operators such as `$ne` or `$gt` to bypass checks.
rules.suggested_fix: Remove `$where`; build filters from validated, type-checked fields (cast ids and numbers explicitly) and reject keys starting with `$`.

rules.title: Template engine auto-escaping turned off
rules.detail: The server-side template engine (Swig, Nunjucks, Handlebars) is configured not to HTML-escape interpolated values, so every template that prints user data becomes a stored or reflected XSS sink.
rules.suggested_fix: Remove the override so auto-escaping stays on, and mark only reviewed, trusted fragments as safe at the call site.

rules.title: Shell command built from dynamic input
rules.detail: A child-process call receives a command string assembled at runtime. If any part comes from a user, an LLM, or a file name, shell metacharacters can run arbitrary commands.
rules.suggested_fix: Prefer a library API over a shell; otherwise use execFile/spawn with a fixed binary and an argument array (no shell: true) and validate arguments against an allow-list.

positive.text:
const cp = require('child_process');
cp.execSync('git log ' + branch);

rules.title: eval or Function constructor on dynamic input
rules.detail: Code is evaluated from a non-literal string. When the string can contain user input or model output, this is remote code execution.
rules.suggested_fix: Replace eval with JSON.parse for data, a lookup table for dispatch, or a sandboxed interpreter; never evaluate LLM output.

rules.title: HTML inserted without sanitization
rules.detail: Markup is written into the DOM through a raw-HTML sink and no sanitizer is referenced in the file. User content or model output rendered this way can run script in your users' sessions.
rules.suggested_fix: Render text with framework bindings or textContent; if HTML is required, sanitize with DOMPurify (or rehype-sanitize for Markdown) immediately before the sink.

rules.title: JWT verification accepts the none algorithm
rules.detail: The accepted algorithm list includes `none`, so unsigned tokens pass verification and anyone can forge a session.
rules.suggested_fix: Pin a single expected algorithm (e.g. `algorithms: ["HS256"]` or `["RS256"]`) and never include none.

rules.title: JWT decoded without signature verification on the server
rules.detail: A token from the incoming request is decoded but not verified in the same file. Decoding only base64-parses the payload; claims such as sub or role can be forged.
rules.suggested_fix: Verify the signature, issuer, audience and expiry (jwt.verify, jose jwtVerify, or supabase.auth.getUser) before trusting any claim.

positive.text:
import { decodeJwt } from 'jose';
export function middleware(request: NextRequest) { const c = decodeJwt(request.cookies.get('t')!.value); }

negative.text:
import { jwtVerify } from 'jose';
export async function middleware(request: NextRequest) { await jwtVerify(t, key); }

rules.title: Passwords hashed with a fast or weak function
rules.detail: Passwords are hashed with a general-purpose hash (MD5/SHA family) or bcrypt with a work factor below 10. Leaked hashes of this kind are cracked quickly.
rules.suggested_fix: Use Argon2id (m=19 MiB, t=2, p=1) or scrypt; if bcrypt is required, use a work factor of 10 or more. Better: delegate passwords to your auth provider.

rules.title: MD5 or SHA-1 used
rules.detail: MD5 and SHA-1 are broken for security purposes. This is fine for cache keys or checksums, but not for signatures, tokens, passwords or integrity checks against an attacker.
rules.suggested_fix: Confirm the use is non-security; otherwise switch to SHA-256 or stronger (or HMAC-SHA-256 for integrity with a key).

rules.title: Math.random used for a security value
rules.detail: Math.random is not cryptographically secure; tokens, codes and IDs derived from it can be predicted.
rules.suggested_fix: Use crypto.randomBytes, crypto.randomUUID or crypto.getRandomValues (crypto.randomInt for numeric codes).

rules.title: Cookie security flag explicitly disabled
rules.detail: A cookie or session is configured with HttpOnly or Secure turned off, letting scripts read the session token or sending it over plain HTTP.
rules.suggested_fix: Set `httpOnly: true, secure: true, sameSite: "lax"` (or "strict") and prefer the `__Host-` cookie name prefix.

negative.text: app.use(session({ secret, cookie: { httpOnly: true, secure: true } }));
nodemailer.createTransport({ host, port: 587, secure: false }); // session

rules.title: Auth token stored in unprotected client storage
rules.detail: Session tokens or secrets are written to localStorage/sessionStorage (readable by any script, so one XSS steals them) or to React Native AsyncStorage (unencrypted on device).
rules.suggested_fix: On the web, keep sessions in HttpOnly Secure cookies; in React Native/Expo, use expo-secure-store or the Keychain/Keystore.

rules.title: TLS certificate verification disabled
rules.detail: Certificate validation is turned off (or an iOS trust challenge is answered without evaluating the server trust), so anyone on the network path can impersonate the server and read or alter traffic.
rules.suggested_fix: Remove the override. For self-signed internal services, pin or add the specific CA instead; on iOS call SecTrustEvaluateWithError before creating URLCredential(trust:).

negative.text:
guard SecTrustEvaluateWithError(trust, nil) else { return }
completionHandler(.useCredential, URLCredential(trust: trust))

rules.title: App Transport Security allows cleartext HTTP
rules.detail: Info.plist disables App Transport Security globally or for a domain, allowing unencrypted HTTP connections that can be read or modified on public Wi-Fi.
rules.suggested_fix: Remove the exception and use HTTPS everywhere; if a specific legacy host is unavoidable, scope a per-domain exception and document why (App Review asks).

rules.title: Hardcoded http:// URL in iOS code
rules.detail: The app references a plain-HTTP endpoint. Traffic to it is unencrypted (or fails under ATS).
rules.suggested_fix: Switch the endpoint to https://.

rules.title: Sensitive value stored in UserDefaults
rules.detail: UserDefaults (and SwiftUI @AppStorage, which wraps it) is an unencrypted plist included in device backups. Tokens and credentials stored there can be extracted.
rules.suggested_fix: Store tokens and secrets in the Keychain (e.g. via a small Keychain wrapper or the Supabase/Firebase SDK session storage).

rules.title: Sensitive value written to logs
rules.detail: A credential-like variable is interpolated into a log statement. Logs are copied to consoles, crash tools and log services with wider access than the secret itself.
rules.suggested_fix: Remove the value from the message or log a redacted form (last 4 characters, a hash, or a boolean).

rules.title: iOS app has no privacy manifest
rules.detail: Swift/Objective-C code uses APIs Apple classifies as required-reason APIs (UserDefaults, file timestamps, system boot time, disk space, active keyboards), but the repository contains no PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy. App Store Connect rejects such uploads since May 1, 2024.
rules.suggested_fix: Add PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy to the app target declaring NSPrivacyAccessedAPITypes with the matching reason codes (e.g. CA92.1 for app-only UserDefaults), plus collected data types and tracking domains.
rules.algorithm: Report once per scan when at least one pattern matches in a Swift/Objective-C file and no walked file has basename PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy. Evidence: every matching line (cap at 20).

rules.title: pull_request_target workflow checks out untrusted PR code
rules.detail: pull_request_target runs with repository secrets and a write token, and this workflow checks out the pull request head. Anyone opening a PR can run code with those privileges (poisoned pipeline execution).
rules.suggested_fix: Use `pull_request` for building untrusted code; if pull_request_target is required, never check out or execute the PR head in that job.

positive.text:
on: pull_request_target
jobs:
  b:
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}

negative.text:
on: pull_request
jobs:
  b:
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}

rules.title: Untrusted event text interpolated into a workflow
rules.detail: Attacker-controlled event text (issue or PR titles, branch names, comments) is expanded by `${{ }}` before the shell runs, so a crafted title can execute commands with the workflow token and secrets.
rules.suggested_fix: Pass the value through an environment variable (`env: TITLE: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}`) and reference "$TITLE" in the script.

positive.text:
on: issues
jobs:
  t:
    steps:
      - run: echo "${{ github.event.issue.title }}"

negative.text:
jobs:
  t:
    steps:
      - env:
          TITLE: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}
        run: echo "$TITLE"

rules.title: Workflow token has write-all permissions
rules.detail: The GITHUB_TOKEN is granted write access to every scope, so any compromised step can push code, create releases or alter settings.
rules.suggested_fix: Set `permissions: contents: read` at the top level and grant specific write scopes only to the jobs that need them.

rules.title: Third-party action not pinned to a commit SHA
rules.detail: A third-party action is referenced by a tag or branch, which its owner (or an attacker who compromises it) can repoint to new code that runs with your secrets.
rules.suggested_fix: Pin to the full 40-character commit SHA and keep a version comment, e.g. `uses: owner/action@<sha> # v2.1.0`; let Dependabot update it.

rules.title: Secret baked into a Docker image
rules.detail: ENV and ARG values are stored in image layers and history, so anyone who can pull the image can read the secret.
rules.suggested_fix: Use BuildKit secret mounts (`RUN --mount=type=secret`) at build time and inject runtime secrets from the orchestrator.

rules.title: MCP server launched from an unpinned package
rules.detail: An MCP server is started with `npx -y <package>` and no version, so each launch runs whatever the registry currently serves for that name, with the agent's tool permissions.
rules.suggested_fix: Pin an exact version (`<package>@1.2.3`), review the server before upgrading, and keep tokens out of the config file.

rules.title: postMessage sent to any origin
rules.detail: Messages posted with target origin `*` are delivered to whatever page currently occupies the window, including an attacker's.
rules.suggested_fix: Pass the exact expected origin, and check `event.origin` in every message listener.

rules.title: Third-party script loaded without integrity check
rules.detail: A script is loaded from another origin without Subresource Integrity, so a compromise of that CDN or vendor runs arbitrary code in your pages.
rules.suggested_fix: Pin a version and add `integrity="sha384-…" crossorigin="anonymous"`, or self-host the file. Dynamic vendor loaders that cannot use SRI belong in your privacy disclosures and CSP allow-list.

rules.title: Production browser source maps enabled
rules.detail: Next.js publishes original source for every client bundle, exposing comments, internal routes and any secrets that slipped into client code.
rules.suggested_fix: Remove productionBrowserSourceMaps or upload maps privately to your error tracker instead.

rules.title: File upload handler without a size limit
rules.detail: The upload middleware accepts files of any size and count, letting one request exhaust disk, memory or storage costs.
rules.suggested_fix: Set `limits: { fileSize, files }`, validate type by extension and magic bytes, and store uploads outside executable paths.

negative.text: const upload = multer({ dest: 'uploads/', limits: { fileSize: 5e6 } });
